name: Week 16 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Lat Pulldown + Incline Curl)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation (the change that kept last pull day flare-free). The DB row pyramid moves to 70/80/90 bare-hand — drop the 60 opener, add a heavier top-end set; grip stays the honest limiter, no straps. Face pull steps to 45 now that the elbows-high cue is locked. Spotlights cycle forward to the lat pulldown and the incline curl — the latter to drill the both-arms-unsupported pattern that finally cleared. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). DB row pyramid → 70/80/90, no straps. Face pull steps to 45. Spotlights cycle to lat pulldown + incline curl. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — last spotlighted W11. Running on the dual pulley at 70 lately, 'very little pain,' grip the limiter at the end. Spotlight drills the wide-grip / bar-to-upper-chest cue and the slow return, and pins down which variant + number to settle on while the shoulder is quiet.

Cycles forward — last spotlighted W13. The weak-left pattern finally cleared — both arms held all sets unsupported with a slow eccentric + bottom pause, a new record. Spotlight drills that both-arms-equal pattern at 25 so it sticks, not just on a good day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W13 bicep + high cable curl + cable crunch · W14 pull-up + DB row · W15 chest-supported row + face pull · W16 lat pulldown + incline curl (current) · W17 cycle forward — chest-supported row + reverse fly refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it kept the last pull day flare-free — it's the protective counter-movement to all the pulling and can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Do it right after the warmup.

**DB row → 70/80/90, no straps.** Drop the 60 opener; the new top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps out first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.

**Grip is the new ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. The shoulder has recovered enough that grip is the honest limiter; no straps.
**Face pull steps to 45** — the elbows-high / external-rotate cue is locked ('feeling it in the back'), so the load can move now.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20, cable crunch pulley 77.5.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. The one flare this cluster was volume/time-under-tension, not weight.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance even though the weak-left finally cleared.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 push warmup + 1-2 KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it kept the last pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort. A light 1-set greasing version also lives in the push + KB-day warmups.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. The limiter now is strength + clean form, not the shoulder; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row + DB Row + Incline Curl (Spotlight) + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides of the chest stay on the pad
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull

**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting up
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze** on the 70/80 sets; the 90 is the heavier top-end set — ~5-6 reps, drive the elbow, control the descent
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. The slower 70/80 sets double as grip work.

**LOAD:** 25lb. 3 sets of 8-10. Preacher-style chest-supported curl (the preacher-bench replacement).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — lock in the both-arms-equal pattern that just cleared:**
- **Set the incline bench to ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad
- **Arm hangs down the face of the pad**, underhand grip; the upper arm stays flat on the pad the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow off)
- **Left arm first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric
- **Both arms unsupported, no spotting hand** — the left held this last time even late in the session; the work is keeping both sides equal in quality

**Reflection:** does the left hold the same clean slow-eccentric + bottom-pause as the right for all 3 sets, even at the end of the block? If it does, the weak-left chapter is closed — the floor has risen.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — strict tempo, cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench)
- DBs hanging fully extended at the start, **soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive**
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep, don't lift
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — keep building the slow drop you've been working

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** ('very little pain' here lately — the current home)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the cue while the shoulder's quiet:**
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- Knees pinned firmly under the pad
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — same as DB row; that's fine, it's the honest cap

**Reflection:** at dual-pulley 70 with the wide grip, does the work stay in the lats (back-pocket squeeze) with the shoulder quiet, or does grip end the set before the lats are done? If grip is consistently the ender, that confirms the shoulder's no longer the ceiling here — settle dual-pulley 70 as the home.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets, Step to 45)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 45 (step up — the cue's locked, the load can move).
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moved the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- Rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of pull day
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 45 drops the elbows, go back to 42.5.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 77.5** (the working number — 'really hard,' slow eccentrics not available here yet)
- **Cable column (rope): ~120**

3 sets.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric where you can** — 77.5 bites hard enough that the slow drop isn't fully available, which means it's the right load. Hold it.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that kept the last pull day flare-free. It can't be the piece a rushed session drops.
**DB row → 70/80/90, no straps.** Drop the 60; new top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it, don't bypass it.
**Spotlight: lat pulldown + incline curl.** Lat pulldown drills the wide-grip / bar-to-chest cue at dual-pulley 70; incline curl drills the both-arms-equal pattern that finally cleared.
**Face pull steps to 45** — the elbows-high cue is locked, so the load can move.
**Grip is the new ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20, cable crunch pulley 77.5.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance.

**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading, which is the change that kept the shoulder quiet. The DB row earns a heavier top-end set with grip — not straps — as the honest cap, by the user's call. Face pull earns its load step now that the cue landed. The spotlights lock in two wins while the shoulder's clear: the lat pulldown cue and the both-arms-equal curl. Building decades, not weeks.
